text: Expand the shipped Python call graph beyond its current v1 boundaries. Add decorated top-level definitions, qualified class-method identities, safe `self`/`cls` resolution, and lexical identities for nested functions in separate increments. Preserve fail-closed behavior for ambiguous instance dispatch, callbacks, dynamic rebinding, and higher-order calls; evaluate type-inference or runtime-trace approaches separately. Reconcile/supersede stale blocked task 082.005-T rather than executing it as written.

Promote Jupyter code cells from content-only retrieval into the code graph using stable virtual source identities such as `notebook.ipynb#cell-0003`. Preserve notebook/cell provenance, resolved cell language, incremental replacement/deletion safety, and search/map/impact parity. Start with cell-isolated parsing; deliberate separately on notebook-wide concatenation and cross-cell symbol resolution because source order is not execution order.

Extend Spark notebook lineage with statically safe increments: delegate literal `spark.sql(...)` strings to the existing SQL extractor, add permanent-view object-kind distinction and DDL expansion, and measure real-corpus recall. Retain authority-bound dataset identities and zero-false-edge fail-closed rules.

Investigate trusted Spark/kernel execution provenance for sound cross-cell DataFrame and temp-view lineage. Model session-scoped ephemeral nodes and bind source identity, isolated Spark session, and execution order; do not authorize graph edges from notebook source order or `execution_count` alone. Keep this separate from static lineage improvements due elevated architecture and runtime-integration scope.

Deepen shipped Power BI intelligence rather than recreating existing DAX edges. Evaluate a distinct measure-dependency edge filter, richer DAX expression/calculated-object lineage, and SQL or Power Query M to Power BI table bridge edges. Retain the current safe lexer seam unless measured consumer needs justify a full DAX AST/semantic engine.

Use `engram eval` on representative real repositories to tune the fixed code-first score gap, measure per-language and content-type retrieval quality, and evaluate graph-aware reranking. Add HNSW or another ANN index only if target-workspace measurements show linear vector search is the bottleneck; preserve keyword-only fallback and honest score reporting.

After the shared HCL parser shipment 117-S lands, deliberate separate semantic increments for `.tf.json`, module/dependency graphs, provider-schema-aware references, and optional plan/state ingestion. Do not fold Terraform evaluation, provider downloads, type inference, or cross-workspace resolution into the syntactic HCL v1 parser.

Decouple MCP initialization and static tools/list availability from full daemon readiness; daemon-dependent calls must return bounded structured startup errors while preserving lifecycle ownership. Traceability: Shipment 118-S, Feature 122-F, review commit 2ef18c0d.

Deliberately upgrade CI Rust/Clippy toolchain from pinned 1.97.0 to 1.98+ and resolve clippy::unused_async_trait_impl. Provenance: PR #346 (feat/123-f-sql-create-procedure-grammar-fork), CI run 32428317557 failed with 78 clippy::unused_async_trait_impl errors under floating stable (resolved to 1.98.0) in pre-existing src/db/cozo_queries.rs, src/server/state.rs, src/shim/transport.rs -- none touched by PR #346. Ship pinned .github/workflows/ci.yml to exact dtolnay/rust-toolchain 1.97.0 (SHA 6c977a6ca4077a0ceb28ffbe03f59d46e9ac8772, master branch per action README) as the narrow deterministic fix so 119-S/123-F could ship on reviewed code. This follow-up must: (1) upgrade the pinned CI toolchain to a deliberately reviewed 1.98+ version, and (2) either redesign the flagged sync-backed async trait impls or make an explicit, reviewed lint-policy decision (allow with justification vs redesign) for clippy::unused_async_trait_impl -- not a blanket unknown_lints/crate-level allow. Not a child of 123-F (completed/archived); independent maintenance unit, does not block 119-S.

Emit degraded-session notification (notifications/message) when shim startup preconditions fail, so supporting MCP clients can surface the condition proactively instead of discovering it only via failed tools/call. Advisory P3 from 124-F (870B1AFF) MCP Protocol Review; not a blocker.

Consider explicit cancellation (e.g. CancellationToken) for the shim's background precondition task (compute_startup_outcome) so the shim can proactively abort readiness/endpoint-derivation work on session end rather than relying solely on ensure_daemon_running's internal budget. Advisory P3 from 124-F (870B1AFF) Concurrency Review; explicitly out of scope for 124-F since it would require touching src/shim/lifecycle.rs.

OPERATOR FOLLOW-UP: during 120-S manual runtime verification, an unscoped 'Get-Process engram,cmd | Stop-Process -Force' was run to clean up a hung manual test, terminating ALL engram.exe and cmd.exe processes visible on the shared host (including several predating the Ship session, as early as 2026-08-15/08-18). No repository/backlog state was affected. Operator should verify whether any other active worktree needs its daemon restarted and whether any closed terminal session needs manual reopening. Full incident note: docs/closure/2026-08-21-870b1aff-runtime-verification.md.

Harden shim startup-failure record path resolution against a TOCTOU race between Path::canonicalize() and cap_std::fs::Dir::open_ambient_dir() in no_follow_diagnostics_dir (src/shim/mod.rs). An attacker with same-user filesystem race capability could replace the workspace root or an ancestor directory between the two calls. Closing this fully would require capability-based directory handles threaded through from a trusted root rather than re-resolving from a path string, a larger architectural change beyond 124-F scope, and this exact canonicalize-then-open pattern is already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. canonicalize_workspace itself). Advisory from 124-F (870B1AFF) Copilot review on PR #349; narrow, same-user-race-only threat model, accepted as a follow-up rather than a 124-F blocker.

Harden shim startup-failure record write against a hard-link attack (src/shim/mod.rs write_startup_failure_record): FollowSymlinks::No plus a regular-file check still accept a pre-created hard link at the leaf path, allowing a process with workspace write access to redirect the append onto a same-filesystem file the operator owns. Validate the opened handle's link count/identity via platform-specific metadata (refuse nlink > 1), or redesign storage to avoid reusing an attacker-provided leaf name entirely (e.g. a fresh per-process/per-timestamp filename). Advisory from 124-F (870B1AFF) Copilot review on PR #349; requires pre-existing workspace write access (same privilege level as many other trusted-workspace-content assumptions already made by the shim/daemon), accepted as a follow-up rather than a 124-F blocker.

Research a CLI-first per-workspace Engram process model. Determine whether each workspace can have exactly one writer/sync process while independent short-lived CLI reader processes query the same workspace without being cancelled, coupled to, or blocked by daemon lifecycle. Evaluate database locking and snapshot consistency, workspace identity and process ownership, IPC versus direct database access, concurrent read/write behavior, Windows and Unix semantics, failure recovery, and observability. Measure effectiveness and resource cost against the current daemon-backed model, define safety invariants for single-writer/multi-reader operation, and recommend whether CLI reads should bypass, coexist with, or coordinate through the daemon. Do not implement until the research establishes a safe architecture.

Durability: fsync the .engram directory after publishing .workspace-id. The hard-link publish syncs file contents but not the parent directory entry, so a Unix crash immediately after first bind can lose the entry and cause the next start to mint a new identity. Not a regression (the previous persist_noclobber path did not fsync the parent either). cap-std 4.0.2 has no Dir::sync_all, but Dir::into_std_file() consumes the capability and exposes the same handle as a std::fs::File whose sync_all() performs a directory fsync, with Dir::reopen_dir() to restore the capability - so this IS reachable without unsafe and without an ambient path. Raised by Copilot review on PR #353.

Test gap: plan 125-F unit U5 requires the handle-identity adversarial scenario to extend to identity persistence, but the deterministic swap tests drive only resolve_git_metadata and resolve_git_branch. Add a hook-driven scenario through load_or_create_workspace_id asserting that attacker-controlled state is neither returned nor written. Raised by Copilot review on PR #353.

Windows: prove the workspace root canonical name denotes the same object as the retained authority handle. Unix does this via handle-derived (dev, ino) in CapRoot::prove_names_same_object; the Windows equivalent (volume serial + file index) is reachable only through cap-primitives' unstable _WindowsByHandle trait or unsafe handle borrowing. Residual is a naming inconsistency, not a false accept. Raised across the 121-S adversarial review and Copilot review on PR #353.

Verify cloud-placeholder reparse tags inside .git are still admitted after the uniform FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT gate (121-S rollback trigger 1). Dehydrated OneDrive/Dropbox files carry the reparse attribute; if a repo under a cloud filter has dehydrated .git contents it may now be rejected where is_symlink() admitted it. LOW confidence, unverified, needs a cloud-backed repository. Primary watch item for the 48-hour observation window.

Compose the workspace proof across multi-value bind call sites. src/tools/lifecycle.rs set_workspace_with_probe calls canonicalize_workspace, workspace_key (daemon key) and resolve_git_branch independently, so each drops its retained root and an ancestor swapped between calls can make the canonical path and branch come from one object while the persisted UUID comes from another. 121-S was freeze-scoped to src/db/workspace.rs and its tests, so this composition fix is deliberately out of that unit. Add a crate-private combined operation returning canonical path, UUID and branch from one GitMetadata/CapRoot and use it at multi-value call sites. Raised by Copilot review on PR #353.

Keep one .engram CapRoot alive across the whole daemon-key decision. daemon_key_for_workspace probes presence through an .engram handle, then workspace_id_from_metadata and read_pid_file_via each reopen .engram from the root, so a substitution between those calls can make the probe inspect one directory while the UUID or live-PID fallback comes from another. Thread a single .engram capability through the probe, identity read, PID read and publish paths. Same family as 1CB366DB. Raised by Copilot review on PR #353.

Refactor Engram to support the latest MCP protocol (currently 2026-07-28) and leverage its capabilities, including native discovery and negotiation, tasks for long-running operations, cacheable deterministic list results, and dual-era compatibility.
